title: This Cat Jumps Nearly 10 Feet Straight Up to Snatch Birds

scenes.text: This cat jumps nearly ten feet straight up from a standstill.
It's a serval, an African wildcat with huge ears and long legs.
It leaps up to three metres high and snatches birds out of the air with its front paws.
Its hunting success rate averages about 50 percent. That's far higher than most cats.
When it hunts rodents, it succeeds 81 percent of the time, pouncing on them across up to four metres.
Nearly ten feet up. Straight up, from standing.

description:
The serval, a long-legged African wildcat, can jump up to 3 metres (nearly 10 feet) straight up to seize birds from the air.
Studies in Ngorongoro found servals succeed in about half of their hunts, and about 81 percent when hunting rodents, far better than most cats.
What is the best jumper you have ever seen, animal or human?
